items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 78:1
items.html: (To the question) Because the Mochin of AB did not come out in the place of the two shoulders of AA, for there is no coupling except in the aspect of the head, and they came out in the place of the GAR of AA, where Aba and Ima stand and are included; and therefore, after Aba and Ima inherited their stature from his GAR, they then bestow the Mochin to ZA, in the way of the clothing of their Yesods, as is known. And all the superiority in the two crowns that ZA inherited is only on the aspect of the inclusion of ZA in them, and therefore he receives from their essentiality. For in the two upper thirds of each one of the HGT of AA, Aba and Ima were included, and in the lower thirds, ZA was included, and therefore they were divided so. However, the Mochin do not come out in the place of the heads of the shoulders of AA, but only in the place of the two upper thirds. And therefore ZA is compelled to receive them, through the clothing of the Yesods of Aba and Ima, through which they are diminished in the second sealing, as above in Answer 208. See there. (Item 115).
